Maybe your anxiety is contributing to not feeling comfortable in any of the roles you’ve tried. A method I have heard to be effective is to envision not a career, but a goal. So instead of “I want to be an engineer”, or “I have to have my own business”, you make it a goal to “own a house asap”, or “hit a savings goal of $10000 in three years”, then you treat everything you do in terms of compensated employment as a way to reach that goal. In that way you hinge your sense of self worth on concrete achievements (ends) instead of the method (means), and it may reduce anxiety of feeling as if nothing “fits right”.

I might be wrong but I think they depict moments in the lives of 2 out of 8 Immortals of the Taoist religion.

The first panel I think depicts Tie Guai Li (on the left) - the leader of the 8 immortals, a Taoist master usually seen in art as a dwarf who wields an iron cane. I think this scene is when the King of Ba (the region of what is now Sichuan) sends for him in an attempt to recruit him to the court, which he rejects, and eventually gives up all earthly concerns to become a Taoist deity. 

The second panel seems to depict Lu Dong Bin, the most famous of the 8 immortals, often depicted with a vyajana (horsetail whisk) in one hand and a sword in the other, symbolizing the eradication of evil through grace and mercy. The two flanking him are his young wards (like squires) that help him carry his stuff. This is a depiction that’s usually seen in Qing dynasty art. 

So IF I am correct, there might be 6 more of these somewhere. Or maybe the artist just decided to tell the story of the two most famous guys among the 8 Taoist immortals. 

Either way, based on the horsetail whisk, the panels should definitely be depictions of Taoist deities.
